experiments.why: A vec3<f64> mix with a splatted f64(1) and an f32 interpolant, whose a and b operands the change now renorms through df64_v3_add; it must still lower and inject df64_v3_mix.
A scalar f64 mix of two raw parameters, whose operands the change newly wraps in df64_add before df64_mix.
A scalar f64 fract of a raw parameter, which the new fract branch renorms through df64_add instead of passing it straight to the helper.
A vec3<f64> normalize of a raw parameter, which now gets a df64_v3_add renorm in front of df64_v3_normalize.
distance between two raw vec3<f64> parameters, whose per-lane df64_sub operands are now each renormed through df64_add.
A vec3<f64> subtraction of two raw parameters, which now renorms both operands through df64_v3_add before df64_v3_sub.
normalize over a sum that is already a df64_v3_add output must not gain a renorm, and abs, min and max must still be injected.

source.quote: returns the SAME module object when no f64 appears anywhere

obligations.statement: fp64Lower(m) returns the very same module object m when no f64 appears anywhere in the module.

source.quote: binops become df64_* calls; helpers + their transitive deps are injected

obligations.statement: Lowering k(a: f64, b: f64) = (a + b) * a keeps the authored function k first in the lowered funcs and injects df64_add among the helper functions.

source.quote: injects the _fp64 guard TEXTURE at (0, 0) when the module declares no bindings

obligations.statement: For a module doing f64 addition that declares no bindings, the lowered module's bindings hold the _fp64 guard texture at group 0, binding 0.

source.quote: only, no emulation, so no guard requirement lands on the host.

obligations.statement: A module whose only f64 use is passing an f64 parameter straight through to another user function (outer(v) calls inner(v), which returns v) lowers with an empty bindings list, so no _fp64 guard is injected.

source.quote: a comparison-ONLY module injects the comparator but NO guard binding

obligations.statement: For k(a: f64, b: f64) = (a < b).select(1.0, 0.0), fp64Lower injects the df64_lt comparator but returns an empty bindings list, with no _fp64 guard binding.

source.quote: an arithmetic op alongside a comparison still injects the guard

obligations.statement: For k(a: f64, b: f64) = ((a + b) < b).select(1.0, 0.0), the lowered module's bindings include the _fp64 guard.

source.quote: a non-whitelisted builtin on f64 operands

obligations.statement: fp64Lower throws an error matching /SD0041/ for a module that applies sin to an f64 operand.

source.quote: binops lower to df64_vN_*; the DF64VecN struct + guard are injected

obligations.statement: Lowering k(a: vec3<f64>, b: vec3<f64>) = (a + b) * a injects df64_v3_add, df64_v3_mul and df64_v3_twoSum among the lowered functions.

source.quote: componentwise builtins lower to df64_vN_* and pull the scalar helpers

obligations.statement: Lowering normalize(abs(a) + min(a, max(a, b))) on vec3<f64> operands injects df64_v3_abs, df64_v3_min and df64_v3_max among the lowered functions.

source.quote: vec64 mix broadcasts a/b operands and takes a SCALAR f32 interpolant only

obligations.statement: Lowering mix(a, f64(1), t) with a: vec3<f64> and a scalar f32 interpolant t succeeds and injects df64_v3_mix.

source.quote: vec64 mix broadcasts a/b operands and takes a SCALAR f32 interpolant only

obligations.statement: fp64Lower throws an error matching /SD0041/ for mix(a, b, t) on vec3<f64> operands when the interpolant t is a vec3<f32> rather than a scalar f32.

source.quote: unsupported builtins / attributes / assigns fail loud

obligations.statement: fp64Lower throws an error matching /SD0041/ for a module that applies sin to a vec3<f64> operand.
